sentences.sentence: The NHS says most coughs are caused by a cold or flu.

sentences.sentence: The NHS cough page lists smoking, heartburn (acid reflux), allergies and infections such as bronchitis as causes.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Persistent coughs can also come from asthma, bronchiectasis, and postnasal drip from hay fever or other nose problems.

sentences.sentence: ACE inhibitors, a type of blood pressure medicine, can cause a long-lasting cough in some people.
sentences.note: Summary 1; page attribution uncertain.

sentences.sentence: For many people the cause of a long-lasting cough is never identified.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says bronchitis usually clears up without treatment in around 3 weeks, and advises seeing a GP if symptoms last longer.

sentences.sentence: A chest infection usually gets better on its own in about 7 to 10 days, although the cough and mucus can last up to 3 weeks.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Antibiotics are generally not used for viral chest infections such as flu or viral bronchitis.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says most coughs can be managed at home with rest and fluids, and a pharmacist can advise on cough medicines.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says there is little evidence on whether over-the-counter cough medicines relieve symptoms.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: An NHS self-care leaflet says stopping or cutting down smoking can help a cough.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS advises seeing a GP if a cough has lasted more than 3 weeks, if weight is being lost for no reason, or if the immune system is weakened.

sentences.sentence: An NHS cancer alliance says a cough is rarely a sign of something serious such as lung cancer, but encourages people with a cough lasting three weeks or more to contact their GP practice so that any serious cause is found early.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: It lists other lung cancer symptoms as coughing up blood, pain when breathing or coughing, persistent breathlessness and persistent tiredness.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS advises an urgent GP appointment or a call to NHS 111 for a cough with chest pain or a feeling of being very unwell.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Coughing up blood and difficulty breathing also need prompt attention, and for trouble breathing the NHS says to call 999.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: For people with bronchiectasis, the NHS says to call 999 if more than a few streaks of blood are coughed up.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A GP will ask how long the cough has lasted and about other symptoms, and may examine the chest.

sentences.sentence: Tests can include a lung function test, a chest X-ray, and a sample of any mucus.

sentences.sentence: Treatment depends on the cause, antibiotics are not normally prescribed for coughs, and a referral to a chest specialist is occasionally needed.
